kicker: Dubai desk · US open 5:30pm Dubai (9:30am ET)
notes: S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time Tuesday on chip-stock strength, but the market retreated Wednesday as the 10-year Treasury yield pushed back toward 5.31% and the 30-year toward 5.68%, keeping rate-sensitive

FOMC minutes from the Sept 15-16 meeting (released Oct 7) reinforced hawkish rate-hike expectations after the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00%; the next decision is Oct 28, with futures still pricing meaningful odds of ano

Oil remains elevated, with Brent trading near/above $100-102 amid an escalating Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict, including recent tanker strikes and rejected diplomatic proposals, keeping energy a relative-strength pocket
Bitcoin broke back below $83,000, extending declines on hawkish Fed minutes and roughly $550 million in leveraged long liquidations, dragging crypto-adjacent equities lower.

Thursday's pre-market tone is defensive: index futures are lower, VIX is up, small caps (IWM/Russell 2000) and industrials are the weakest spots, while Healthcare is showing the best relative strength.

Q3 earnings season is just getting started; the heavy reporting week (big banks, UNH, JNJ) doesn't begin until Oct 13, so today's tape is driven more by macro/yields/oil than by a dense earnings slate.
calendar: Before the open Thursday: PepsiCo (PEP) and Progressive (PGR) report; Tilray (TLRY) and Helen of Troy (HELE) also post results.
8:30am ET Thursday: Initial and Continuing Jobless Claims are the main scheduled U.S. data catalyst.
Friday: Delta Air Lines (DAL) earnings plus preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment.

IPO watch: TRex Bio (TRXB), an Eli Lilly-backed autoimmune/inflammatory biotech, is pricing Oct 8 with a planned Nasdaq debut Oct 9; Retension Pharmaceuticals (RTSN) is also in the pricing window this week.
Next big catalyst week is Oct 13, when JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Citigroup, UnitedHealth and Johnson & Johnson kick off large-cap earnings season.
Next FOMC rate decision is Oct 28, 2026; current fed funds target range is 3.75%-4.00% after September's 25bp hike.

items.name: Constellation Energy
items.news: Constellation climbed after Amazon agreed to buy 690 megawatts of output from its Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant under a 20-year contract tied to more than $3 billion in plant investment. Bloomberg also reported Google is nearing a separate nuclear supply deal with Constellation worth $1 billion or more.
items.risk: Nuclear/AI power-deal enthusiasm is a crowded trade and shares could give back gains quickly on any delay or denial of the rumored Google agreement.
items.entry: Dip to $293.01–297.62, or break above $309.80 on volume

items.name: Flutter Entertainment
items.news: Flutter, the FanDuel parent, rose almost 3% in Wednesday's pre-market after Citi upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral.
items.risk: A single broker upgrade can fade quickly in a risk-off tape, and the stock is sensitive to U.S. sports-betting tax/regulatory headlines.
items.entry: Dip to $73.83–75.25, or break above $78.58 on volume

items.name: Freshworks Inc.
items.news: Freshworks rose nearly 4% in pre-market trading after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the stock will be added to the S&P SmallCap 600 effective before the open on October 8, creating expected passive index-fund buying pressure into the rebalance.
items.risk: Index-inclusion pops can mean-revert once the mechanical buying from tracking funds is complete.

items.name: AbbVie Inc.
items.news: AbbVie shares were reported higher after its drug temab-A earned FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations in colorectal cancer (CRC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), a regulatory catalyst dated October 7.
items.risk: Breakthrough Therapy designation only accelerates the review pathway and does not guarantee eventual approval, limiting the durability of the move.
